newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close lower, foreigners inactive.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close lower, foreigners inactive.

text.p: A lack of fresh news and declines in Wall Street and several Asian markets forced foreigners to switch investments to the foreign exchange market driving down the index with small turnover on Monday, brokers said.

"There's no fresh and good news in the market at all today. Investors weren't active as they switched investment to the foreign exchange market which was more exciting and offered higher returns than the stock market," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
The SET index ended 8.14 points lower at 840.42 on about two billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index slipped 0.74 point to 63.08.

Decliners heavily led gainers 194 to 84 while 97 issues were unchanged. All the major sectors retreated with the banking sector was the most active in terms of value, falling 0.86 percent followed by the finance sector dropping 1.69 percent and the communication sector slipping 0.08 percent.
Brokers said the market was sluggish as investors were also awaiting leading economic indicators to be released by the Bank of Thailand on Thursday.
Brokers said investors focused selling on some large capitalised bank and communication issues and took profits.

Advanced Info Services topped the active list, rising 10 baht to 268. Krung Thai Bank dropped one to 51 while Nava Finance and Securities retreated 0.75 to 39 and Thai Telephone and Telecommunication dropped 0.25 to 29.25.
Ayudhya Jardine CMG Life, in the insurance sector, was among the heavy losers, falling 10.50 baht to 95.50.
Support is seen by some brokers at 830 and resistance at 850 on Tuesday.
